label: Quantum chemistry
title: Electronic structure, with independent references
teaser: Constructed molecular Hamiltonians and benchmarked solver accuracy against basis and active-space choices.
outcome: H₂: |VQE − FCI| < 1.7 × 10⁻⁹ Ha across 7 bond lengths.
motivation: A low variational energy alone does not establish a correct molecular simulation. These studies ask how the Hamiltonian, solver, basis and active space each affect the result.
implementation: H₂ bond scans, an eight-qubit HCN π-active-space VQE study, and nested active-space benchmarks for NH₃, H₂CO₃ and HCO₃⁻. The notebooks expose molecular integrals, fermionic assembly, Jordan–Wigner mapping, state preparation and physical-sector checks. RHF, PBE, FCI and CASCI provide explicitly scoped references.
result: Across seven STO-3G H₂ bond lengths, the saved VQE energies differ from FCI by less than 1.7 × 10⁻⁹ Ha. All nine seeded HCN runs meet the recorded active-space energy target. The scaling study compares 4-, 8- and 12-qubit spaces against the same orbital-basis references.
limitation: These are noiseless, finite-basis calculations. Solver agreement does not remove basis or active-space error. Fixed geometries, a frozen HCN σ framework and the absence of diffuse functions for the anion limit chemical interpretation. No experimental-accuracy or hardware claim is made.
note: The H₂ figure includes nuclear repulsion. FCI is exact within the selected finite basis.
alt: H₂ total energies and signed differences from FCI across seven bond lengths, comparing RHF, PBE, FCI and VQE.
caption: Saved H₂ benchmark: total energies and differences from finite-basis FCI. Figure reproduced from the executed notebook.

label: ADMET
title: Building and testing a quantum pipeline for drug-property modeling
teaser: Developed a molecular-data-to-quantum-circuit pipeline with counterdiabatic control, QSVT and post-measurement learning.
outcome: 1,965 labelled molecules prepared; private execution confirmed.
motivation: A quantum molecular-learning pipeline needs consistent data fitting, Hamiltonian construction, circuit approximation and measurement contracts before its predictive results can be interpreted.
implementation: I developed the ADMET application and, in collaboration with colleagues, the reusable Triple Alpha/Beryllium simulation library. Molecular fingerprints feed information-screened Ising Hamiltonians, molecule-specific counterdiabatic controls and heralded QSVT. Exact-evolution references, scaffold-separated classical controls and a post-measurement readout support the pipeline.
result: The supervised preparation retained 1,965 labelled molecular identities and all 1,975 valid structures for measurement or prediction. Author-confirmed private compilation and execution through Horizon Quantum’s Triple Alpha workflow completed successfully; proprietary outputs remain confidential. Public checks reproduce the disclosed offline pipeline.
limitation: The Hamiltonian is a dimensionless data encoding, not an electronic-structure Hamiltonian or a calibrated biological mechanism. Public quantum ADMET predictive accuracy is not established. First-order counterdiabatic control does not improve fidelity at every tested duration. Public CI does not independently reproduce the private execution.
note: ADMET application developed by Senay Kahsay; reusable simulation library co-developed with colleagues. Full contribution credits are retained in the repository.
alt: Counterdiabatic transport benchmark comparing bare annealing, first-order control and an exact reference at several durations.
caption: Public four-qubit control ablation. This figure is an offline benchmark, separate from the confidential native execution.

label: QFT & order finding
title: Fourier arithmetic with coherent-phase checks
teaser: Implemented a shared Fourier core for reversible arithmetic and bounded Shor order-finding studies.
outcome: Factors 15 with gate-built arithmetic; 21 with a compiled oracle.
motivation: Correct basis-state probabilities can conceal incorrect controlled phases. The study tests whether Fourier arithmetic and phase estimation implement the intended coherent transformations.
implementation: Qiskit and PennyLane share a checked QFT convention. Independent Fourier matrices, FFT states and arithmetic references test addition, multiplication, exponentiation and clean workspace. Continued-fraction candidates are validated modularly without a blind classical order-search fallback.
result: Gate-built QFT modular arithmetic factors 15. A separately labelled compiled-permutation oracle factors 21. The order-6, base-5 example modulo 21 is retained as a negative control because it fails factor extraction despite finding a valid order.
limitation: The N=21 oracle is a small-instance compiled construction, not scalable modular arithmetic. These are ideal bounded simulations. Gate comparisons use all-to-all connectivity and do not establish hardware performance or runtime advantage.
note: Arithmetic correctness, valid order finding and successful factor extraction are distinct outcomes.
alt: Saved Shor order-finding benchmark outcomes and logical resources for bounded instances.
caption: Measured order-finding evidence from the QFT study, with the compiled-oracle boundary retained.

label: QUBO & QAOA
title: Airline recovery under shared capacity constraints
teaser: Measured feasible reallocation and compared local QAOA sampling with classical annealing.
outcome: Mean allocation: 72.19% of bookings; 61.29% of passengers.
motivation: The study examined recovery of disrupted bookings under shared seat inventory and an explicit service-cost objective. The quantum extension was evaluated against the same local QUBOs.
implementation: A whole-booking capacity-slack QUBO, classical simulated annealing, route expansion and audited local improvement act on 7,653 PNRs (booking groups) and 11,822 passengers. QAOA compares structurally selected neighborhoods, one-choice mixers, exact local references and globally checked patch admission.
result: The expanded classical hybrid reallocated 72.19% of bookings and 61.29% of passengers, averaged across five seeds. In the larger local study, depth-4 QAOA recovered the best verified local objective value in 13 of 18 runs, compared with 14 for annealing. QAOA added zero bookings or passengers; exact enumeration confirmed local allocation saturation.
limitation: Local QAOA results are not full-population reallocation rates. Independent patches cannot be summed. Each exact local Pareto frontier has one nondominated point. No quantum advantage is established; the airline’s Gurobi comparison remains external.
note: PNR/passenger allocation and valid-sample counts have different denominators and are reported separately.
alt: QAOA and annealing optimum-discovery counts, alongside exact local booking-allocation ceilings.
caption: Larger-neighborhood QAOA study. The equal incumbent and exact-maximum bars establish the local allocation limit.

label: Electricity-grid forecasting
title: Quantum reservoirs against strong classical controls
teaser: Benchmarked continuous-variable and analogue-spin reservoirs with chronological evaluation and resource accounting.
outcome: 324.3 MW RMSE: gradient boosting; ≈351.0 MW: quantum hybrids.
motivation: Test whether verified quantum reservoir features add forecasting value once data timing, model selection and classical feature access are controlled.
implementation: Two bosonic modes use Gaussian/Kerr ablations and Fock-cutoff checks; six interacting spins use exact dynamics and independent Qiskit references. Expanding validation folds select models before a fixed test interval. Persistence, seasonal forecasts, ridge, random forest, gradient boosting and a classical reservoir provide matched controls.
result: Across 2,823 held-out targets, gradient boosting reaches 324.3 MW RMSE. Both Kerr-hybrid and interacting-spin-hybrid ensembles reach approximately 351.0 MW; persistence reaches 806.4 MW. Verified quantum dynamics and resource estimates are retained alongside this negative predictive-advantage result.
limitation: This is a historical 30-minute-ahead hindcast, not an operational forecast. One geographic series and seasonal holdout do not establish general superiority. Routing, calibration and hardware noise are not modelled; seed spread and temporal uncertainty do not guarantee absence of overfitting.
note: Based on the QUAC 605 collaborative project. Full contribution credits are retained in the repository.
alt: Analogue-spin reservoir forecasting results compared with classical baselines and resource diagnostics.
caption: Saved benchmark. Demand data: National Energy SO, NESO Open Licence. Original collaboration is credited in the project guide.

label: Bioinformatics
title: A modular genomic-ancestry workflow
teaser: Connected contamination estimates, principal components and reference-population assignment in a Snakemake workflow.
outcome: A modular workflow for genomic quality control and population assignment.
motivation: The project brought ancestry-related quality control and population assignment into one modular workflow, with explicit reference resources and sample alignment.
implementation: The workflow connects GRCh38 preparation and VerifyBamID2 outputs to contamination tables, harmonized principal components, a four-PC K-nearest-neighbor classifier and PCA visualizations. Python tests cover table alignment, PC-column parsing and a small synthetic assignment case.
result: The repository implements the processing stages and synthetic reference tests. Its outputs are contamination summaries, aligned PC tables, population-label tables and plots. No cohort-level accuracy or benchmark measurements are published here.
limitation: Reference genomes, compatible 1000 Genomes resources and authorized sample inputs are required for a full run. No individual genomic records are displayed.

label: Reusable classical learning
title: Learning models that connect the studies
teaser: Developed reusable forecasting and molecular-classification APIs for grid benchmarking and ADMET.
outcome: Reusable Python models with explicit data and evaluation contracts.
motivation: Classical comparisons need reusable implementations with consistent fitting, evaluation and inference.
implementation: Ridge, random forest, gradient boosting and echo-state reservoirs support the grid study. Full- and selected-count logistic classifiers support molecular ADMET learning. The extracted modules expose training, prediction, chronological or scaffold-separated evaluation, and portable molecular-model inference.
result: The standalone forecasting run reproduces 324.3 MW test RMSE for gradient boosting on 2,823 targets. Molecular tests verify preprocessing, partition separation and portable inference; no ADMET predictive accuracy is claimed.
limitation: Forecasting uses one historical geographic series. Molecular callers supply prepared features and scaffold keys; correct upstream preprocessing remains essential. These are the classical controls from the linked studies, packaged for independent reuse.

label: Monte Carlo estimation
title: Accuracy under a fixed sampling budget
teaser: Compared Monte Carlo and randomized quasi-Monte Carlo under equal option-pricing sampling budgets.
motivation: How much estimator error remains when every method receives the same number of payoff evaluations?
implementation: Plain Monte Carlo, antithetic normals and scrambled Sobol/Halton sequences estimate discounted European-call payoffs. Three synthetic contracts, four budgets, four outer seeds and sixteen independent replications are checked against Black–Scholes.
result: At 131,072 payoff evaluations per estimate, at-the-money price RMSE across four seeds is 0.000459 for Sobol and 0.0332 for plain Monte Carlo. Antithetic pairs count as two evaluations.
limitation: Results concern one-dimensional, constant-volatility risk-neutral GBM with zero dividends. Replication-based intervals are approximate. These observations do not establish general pricing superiority or market-prediction accuracy.
note: RMSE is measured in option-price units across four retained seeds. This is numerical estimation, not a trained predictive model.
alt: Saved option-price estimation RMSE across four seeds versus equal total payoff budgets for Monte Carlo, antithetic, scrambled Sobol and Halton methods.
caption: Matched sampling budgets for three synthetic contracts. Curves show observed error, not a guaranteed convergence rate.

label: Multiobjective optimization
title: Cost–emissions tradeoffs with an exact reference
teaser: Compared MOPSO and classical QPSO against exact references for constrained unit commitment.
motivation: Can population-based methods recover cost–emissions tradeoffs while preserving feasible generation schedules?
implementation: Two generators meet four hourly demands with explicit commitment, startup and output constraints. Both methods use 4,530 candidates per run and five fixed seeds. An analytic Pareto line and seventeen independent HiGHS MILPs provide references.
result: Median normalized dominated hypervolume is 0.7020 for MOPSO and 0.6758 for QPSO, against 0.71 for the continuous reference front. Every retained schedule passes the independent feasibility audit.
limitation: The synthetic model excludes ramping, minimum up/down times, reserves and network constraints. Hypervolume depends on the declared normalization and reference point. QPSO executes classically; this small study does not establish universal optimizer rankings.
note: Hypervolume measures tradeoff coverage, not an allocation percentage. Quantum-inspired QPSO does not use a quantum backend.
alt: MOPSO and QPSO fronts compared with the exact cost-emissions Pareto line and convergence of normalized dominated hypervolume.
caption: Fixed budgets and seeds; convergence bands span the observed seed range.

label: Supporting study
title: Fuzzy resource allocation
teaser: Evaluated robust production decisions under triangular profit and resource uncertainty.
outcome: An uncertainty-aware allocation model with an independent LP reference.
motivation: The study examined resource allocation when factory profits and available quantities were uncertain.
implementation: Alpha-cut linear programs compare robust, nominal, optimistic and original policies. Independent feasible-vertex enumeration checks the HiGHS solutions.
result: Robust objective profit increases from 90.45 to 105.0 as alpha goes from zero to one; all thirty-six cases match the independent objective reference.
limitation: Synthetic two-product model. Alpha denotes fuzzy membership, not probability; policy objectives use different coefficients.
note: A small supporting uncertainty study; no carbon-storage or probabilistic-confidence claim.
